8-152. Military Occupational Specialties
MOS 152B--OH-58A/C Scout Pilot; 152C--OH-6 Pilot; 152D--OH-58D Pilot; 152E—AH-64E Pilot;
152F--AH-64A Attack Pilot; 152H--AH-64D Attack Pilot.
   a. Licensing/certification requirements. None.
   b. Prerequisites. DA Cir 601 series.
   c. MOS 152C is a non-accession MOS. MOS 152B, 152D, 152E, 152F, and 152H are accession MOS
with all enlisted MOS performing as feeder MOS. MOS 152B, 152D, 152E, 152F, and 152H may be
substituted for MOS 153A CW5 positions at all levels.
   d. Associated SQI.
        (1) 0--No special qualifications.
        (2) 8--Instructor.
        (3) B--Aviation Safety Officer.
        (4) C--Instructor Pilot.
        (5) F--Senior Instructor Pilot and Instrument Flight Examiner.
        (6) G--Aviation Maintenance Officer.
        (7) H--Standardization Instructor Pilot.
        (8) I--Tactical Operations Officer.
        (9) L--Maintenance Test Flight Evaluator.
        (10) P--Parachutist.
        (11) T--Transition (personnel only).
        (12) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Officer.
   e. Associated ASI. (Refer to table 6-6 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all warrant officer
MOS)).
        (1) 5A--Joint Air Tactical Operations Officer.
        (2) 5U--Air Operations Officer.
        (3) A2--OH-58A/C Scout Pilot (not for use with positions coded with MOS 152B).
        (4) B4--UH-72A Pilot.
        (5) D7--AH-64D (for use with positions coded with MOS 152H and 153A only).
        (6) D8 – Government Flight Representative (GFR) (for use with positions coded with MOS 152E
and 152H only).
        (7) D9--AH-64E Pilot (for use with positions coded with MOS 153A).
        (8) G2--Instructor Pilot (not for use with positions coded with SQI C).
        (9) G7--Aviation Related.
        (10) G8--Aviation Safety Officer (not for use with positions coded with SQI B).
        (11) H2--Aviation Life Support Equipment Officer.
        (12) H8--Master Gunner.
        (13) K2 – SOA AH-6 (Attack) Pilot for use with 152C only (Effective 202510 Personnel only,
Effective 202610 Personnel and Positions).
        (14) K3 – SOA MH-6 (Assault) Pilot for use with 152C only (Effective 202510 Personnel only,
Effective 202610 Personnel and Positions).
        (15) K4--Special Operations Aviation (indicates OH/MH/AH-6 Pilot when used in conjunction with
MOS 152C).
        (16) Q6--Protection Cell Operations (personnel only) (for use with MOS 152C, 152E and 152H)
(Effective 202410).
   f. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial awarding of MOS 152BCDEFH
        (1) WO1/CW2 must--
              (a) Be a U.S. citizen. Qualify for a security eligibility of SECRET.
              (b) Meet medical qualifications. WO1 and CW2 must--
                    1. Initially meet the medical examination requirements of Class I medical standards as
prescribed by AR 40-501.
                    (a) A physical demand Rating of “Moderate” (Gold)
                    (b) A physical profile of 111121
                    (c) Color discrimination of red/green
                    (d) Correctable distant vision acuity 20/50 near vision acuity Correctable 20/20 in each
eye.
                    (e) Qualifying Scores
                        (1) A minimum OPAT score of Long Jump (LJ)-0120cm,Seated Power Throw (PT)-
0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036 shuttles in Physical
Demand Category in “Moderate” (Gold).
                        (2) 40 or above on Selection Instrument for Flight Test (SIFT)
                    2. Maintain Class II medical standards once an officer is on flight status.
              (c) Maintain height and weight standards per AR 600-9 and AR 40-501.
              (d) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Technical Certification Course (IERW for152).
              (e) Successfully complete the appropriate aircraft qualification training.
              (f) Be commissioned upon promotion to CW2.
        (2) CW3 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f (1) above.
              (b) Successfully complete the Aviation Warrant Officer Advanced Course (AVWOAC).
        (3) CW4 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f(2) above unless awarded ASI G7 through board
action.
              (b) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Staff Course (WOSC).
        (4) CW5 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f(3) above unless awarded ASI G7 through board
action.
              (b) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Senior Staff Course (WOSSC).
   g. Duties.
        (1) WO1/CW2--
              (a) Plans flights, ascertains factors such as load, weight, fuel supply, route, altitudes or
schedules as necessary to safely accomplish mission.
              (b) Supervises loading and unloading of aircraft to ensure load stability, balance and
adherence to aircraft load limitations.
              (c) Pilots and commands assigned aircraft under tactical and non-tactical conditions for
military purposes.
              (d) Conducts pre/post-tactical mission briefings.
              (e) Performs aerial evasive maneuvers.
              (f) Trains personnel to engage hostile forces with aircraft armament systems.
              (g) Maintains Aircrew Training Program requirements in appropriate aircraft.
              (h) Detects satisfactory and unsatisfactory aircraft system or flight performance.
              (i) Executes emergency operating procedures for assigned aircraft.
        (2) CW3--
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1)(a) through (n) above.
              (b) Manages maintenance personnel, tech supply, ground support equipment and facility
assets to maintain, repair, test fly, and recover rotary wing aircraft.
        (3) CW4--
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1)(a) through (b) above.
              (b) As an IP, ASO or MTP in Special Operations Aviation also performs duties described in
paragraph g(2)(c) through (h).
        (4) CW5--
              (a) Performs duties required in paragraph g(1)(a) through (b).
              (b) As a SIP, ASO, MTFE or tactical operations officer in Special Operations Aviation.
   h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
        (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate.
        (2) Table 8-152BCDEFH-1. Physical requirements.
        (3) Authorized titles are provided in tables 6-2 and 6-3. The following grades are used to code
positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4;
and W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the following standards of grade tables:

             (5) Table 8-152D-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
